title: Build the Residence Label and Values

lessons.title: ਰ (ra) — one new base for the residence label

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — one tiny step until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Find the familiar short-vowel mark ਿ. Today adds only one base letter.
Trace ਰ slowly twice. Say ra. Then place ਿ before it once: ਰਿ.
Write ਰ (ra) once without the model. Compare only the base shape and repair one difference.
Stop after this one new base.

segments.prompt: Which new Gurmukhi base letter did you trace for ra?

feedback.incorrect: Trace ਰ once more, then stop.

lessons.title: ਇ — one independent vowel
lessons.gloss: trace the independent Gurmukhi vowel i

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — one tiny step until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Write the new base ਰ (ra) once. Leave a finger-width of space beside it.
Trace ਇ slowly twice. It stands on its own; it is not the attached mark ਿ.
Point to ਇ, cover it, and write it once. Repair only the new shape.
No word is scored yet.

segments.prompt: Which independent Gurmukhi vowel did you trace today?

feedback.incorrect: Compare ਇ with the attached mark ਿ, then try once more.

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — one label until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Touch the pieces in order: ਰਿ, ਹਾ, ਇ, ਸ਼.
Join ਰਿ + ਹਾ + ਇ + ਸ਼ = ਰਿਹਾਇਸ਼ (rihāish). On a form, ਰਿਹਾਇਸ਼ (rihāish) labels the residence line. Copy the label once and leave its answer blank.
Point to the label and say what information belongs there. Do not add a value yet.
The familiar spoken word ਰਹਿਣਾ can remind you of living somewhere; only the form label is scored here.

segments.prompt: A form shows ਰਿਹਾਇਸ਼ (rihāish). What information belongs on that line?

lessons.title: ਡ (ḍa) — one new base for a residence value

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — one tiny step until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Find the familiar nasal mark ੰ. Today adds one base letter beneath the line.
Trace ਡ slowly twice. Say ḍa. Do not build the whole word yet.
Cover the model and write ਡ (ḍa) once. Repair only the base shape.
One new base is enough.

segments.prompt: Which new Gurmukhi base letter did you trace for dda?

feedback.incorrect: Trace ਡ once more, then stop.

lessons.title: ਪਿੰਡ (piṇḍ) — assemble one residence value
lessons.gloss: village as a neutral residence value

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — one value until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Touch ਪ, then the pre-base ਿ, then ੰ, then ਡ (ḍa).
Build ਪਿ + ੰ + ਡ (ḍa) = ਪਿੰਡ (piṇḍ). It means “village.” Copy ਪਿੰਡ (piṇḍ) once.
Cover the model, say the meaning, and write the value once. Reveal it and repair one piece.
Only this value is scored today.

segments.prompt: Copy the Gurmukhi residence value meaning village.

feedback.incorrect: Rebuild ਪਿ + ੰ + ਡ, then compare once.

lessons.title: ਸ਼ਹਿਰ (shahir) — assemble the other residence value
lessons.gloss: city as a neutral residence value

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script — one value until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Touch the known pieces ਸ਼, ਹਿ, ਰ (ra) in order.
Join ਸ਼ + ਹਿ + ਰ (ra) = ਸ਼ਹਿਰ (shahir). It means “city.” Copy ਸ਼ਹਿਰ (shahir) once.
Cover the model, say the meaning, and write the value once. Repair only the first differing piece.
The two values remain separate until the next lesson.

segments.prompt: Copy the Gurmukhi residence value meaning city.

feedback.incorrect: Rebuild ਸ਼ + ਹਿ + ਰ, then compare once.

lessons.title: The wellbeing exchange returns at R4
lessons.romanization: kivēṁ — tusī̃ kivēṁ ho — maiṁ ṭhīk hāṁ — koī gall nahīṁ
lessons.gloss: retrieve every Chapter 3 wellbeing atom at R4

segments.text: No new language. Keep this oral: listen, speak, then type only a record of what you already said.
Ask, answer, and close once. Romanization records prior speech only; it earns no Gurmukhi reading or writing credit.

segments.prompt: Hear tusī̃ kivēṁ ho? Give its meaning aloud, then name respectful ho and the k-question-family sound.

feedback.incorrect: Listen once more, then answer from meaning.

segments.prompt: Reply I am fine aloud, then name maiṁ's first-person m-family.

feedback.incorrect: Say maiṁ ṭhīk hāṁ, then keep the opening m-.

segments.prompt: Answer thanks with no problem aloud, then name nahīṁ's negative n-family.

feedback.correct: The courtesy close returned at R4.
feedback.incorrect: Say koī gall nahīṁ, then keep the opening n-.

segments.text: Say the three-turn exchange once more from meaning alone.
